## Bogota in 5 hours: La Candelaria, museums and Monserrate

[Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) sits high in the Andes. A single city excursion introduces you to colonial architecture, the legacy of pre-Hispanic cultures and twentieth-century art, before offering views of the capital from Mount Monserrate.

Our city tour lasts **5 hours**. Hotel departure is scheduled for **9:00**, with **transfers and an English-speaking guide included**; lunch is paid for separately. The order of visits may be changed if necessary to accommodate museum opening hours and road conditions.

## La Candelaria and Plaza Bolivar

The excursion begins in **La Candelaria**, Bogota's historic district, where colonial-era buildings, squares and cultural institutions survive. Narrow streets, contrasting facades and street-art projects quickly convey the atmosphere of the old city.

One landmark on the route is **Plaza Bolivar**. It is surrounded by major administrative and religious buildings, including the cathedral, Palace of Justice and other monuments of the city centre. The programme also mentions Casa de Nariño and Liévano Palace.

A visit to the square offers a chance to see the facades and understand the buildings' historical roles. **Access to the interiors of government institutions should not be assumed to be part of the standard excursion without separate arrangements.**

## Gold Museum: Colombia's pre-Hispanic cultures

The itinerary includes the **Gold Museum**, managed by Banco de la República, Colombia's central bank. It preserves one of the most important collections of pre-Columbian goldwork, with tens of thousands of objects made of gold and other materials by cultures from what is now Colombia.

The exhibits help explain why gold held significance in ancient societies far beyond the metal's material value. Jewellery, ceremonial objects and symbolic images reveal aspects of social life, religion and craftsmanship. Among the best-known subjects is the Muisca culture, closely associated with the legend of El Dorado.

The museum closes on certain days of the week, and access to particular galleries changes occasionally. The **actual order of visits** must therefore take its opening schedule into account. A specific entrance-ticket rate is not separately confirmed as an included service on this excursion.

## Botero Museum and Casa de la Moneda

The next part visits Bogota's cultural quarter, including the **Botero Museum** and **Casa de la Moneda**. Fernando Botero became renowned for his distinctive depictions of people and objects. His paintings and sculptures provide a very different perspective on Colombia's history and identity from the archaeological artefacts at the Gold Museum.

Several museums close together make for a rewarding route, but its **five-hour duration** requires sensible time management. You cannot see every room in every collection on one outing. The guide helps focus attention on significant works and their historical context.

## Monserrate: Bogota from above

The programme ends with **an ascent of Monserrate**, the mountain above central Bogota. Viewpoints offer panoramas of the capital's neighbourhoods and the surrounding mountains. On a clear day, the city's position on a high-altitude plateau is particularly evident.

The ascent follows the current regulations and operating arrangements for transport on Monserrate. We include a visit to the mountain, but no separate cable car or funicular fare is specified, so the means of ascent should be confirmed before the excursion.

Mountain weather changes rapidly. Bring a light jacket, a raincoat and shoes suitable for walking on paved paths.

Transfers and an English-speaking guide are included; lunch is separate. These prices reflect the terms of our excursion; when choosing a particular date, museum access must be confirmed.

For further exploration of the capital, consider the [Zipaquira and Lake Guatavita excursion](/colombia/bogota/zipaquira-guatavita-tour-from-bogota/), focusing on ancient traditions and underground architecture.

### What time does the excursion start?

Hotel departure is scheduled for **9:00**, and the total duration is **5 hours**.

### Which museums are on the itinerary?

The Gold Museum, Botero Museum and Casa de la Moneda.

### Does the tour include Monserrate?

Yes. The itinerary ends with an ascent of Monserrate and a view over the city.

### Is lunch included?

No. Lunch is paid for separately.

### How much does the trip cost for a couple?

**$141 per person** for a group of 2.

## Colombia tours featuring a Bogota sightseeing excursion

The [five-hour Bogota city tour](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/) introduces historic La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, the Botero collection, Plaza Bolivar and views of the city from Monserrate. It is a good starting point for a journey through Colombia: first the capital's culture, then mountain scenery, coffee plantations and the Caribbean Sea.

Here you will find {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring this excursion. Their main difference is **how many other regions you can visit after Bogota**, and which flights, hotels and services are included in the selected package.

## Five to eleven days: how the itineraries differ

On the [five-day "Bogota and Cartagena" programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/), the city tour takes place on arrival day. Next come [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquira](/colombia/place/zipaquira/), followed by Cartagena and relaxation near the Rosario Islands. It suits a short holiday focused on history and the coast.

The [seven-day "Bogota, Medellin and Cartagena" tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) adds Medellin and a trip to Guatapé while retaining the capital and the Caribbean coast. The [nine-day "Colombia in Four Chapters"](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) covers more coffee-growing and urban destinations, while the [11-day "Many Faces of Colombia"](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) includes a coffee farm, San Andrés and other regions.

|---|---|
| [5 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) | Cartagena, Rosario Islands |
| [7 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) | Medellin, Guatapé |
| [9 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-explorer-9-days/) | Coffee region |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_colombia_essential_5_days,tour_colombia_highlights_7_days,tour_colombia_explorer_9_days,tour_colombia_complete_11_days}}

All these programmes provide a chance to start exploring Colombia in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). However, paid services and flight arrangements differ, so read the detailed conditions on each tour's own page.

## What the five-hour city tour covers

The standalone excursion begins in the historic La Candelaria district. The route includes the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda, Botero Museum and Plaza Bolivar, followed by an ascent of Monserrate for views of the city. The duration is **5 hours**, with hotel departure at 09:00.

| Stop | What you will see |
|---|---|
| La Candelaria | Historic neighbourhoods |
| Museums | Gold, Botero collection |
| Plaza Bolivar | Main buildings of the centre |
| Monserrate | Panorama of Bogota |

Under the terms of the [standalone excursion](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/), transfers and an English-speaking guide are included, but lunch is not. It has a separate price table based on group size; those prices apply to standalone bookings and not automatically to every multi-day tour.

Museum visits depend on opening hours. If the excursion falls on a day when one attraction is closed, the order of visits and possible changes must be agreed in advance.

## Five or six hours: why the excursions must not be confused

We also offer a [six-hour private programme featuring museums and Monserrate](/colombia/bogota/bogota-museums-monserrate-6-hours/). It overlaps with the five-hour city tour at several sites, but differs in duration and inclusions: the six-hour option specifically lists museum tickets, the Monserrate ascent and a local medical insurance card.

These are two separate products. If a multi-day tour lists "Bogota, museums and Monserrate", check which excursion module it actually includes. That way you avoid mistakenly expecting tickets and additional services that belong to another excursion.

## Coordinating the city tour with arrival and transfers

Some itineraries schedule the city tour **on arrival day**. In that case, flight landing time, passport control, the drive from El Dorado Airport and the start of the excursion must be compatible. A long international flight should also be considered when deciding how busy to make the first day.

Compare domestic airfare separately. For example, on the [five-day programme](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/), the Bogota–Cartagena flight is listed among separately payable items. Do not judge the package by its minimum price alone without checking transport costs and accommodation category.

If history is your main interest, start with our [cultural and historical tours of Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/). For the complete choice of destinations, see the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring the Bogota city excursion

### How long does the sightseeing excursion take?

The standalone Bogota city tour lasts 5 hours. In multi-day itineraries, departure times are coordinated with arrival and other activities.

### What language is the excursion conducted in?

The five-hour excursion is conducted in English. Other guiding languages must be confirmed in the terms of the particular tour.

### Is lunch included?

No. Lunch is not included in the five-hour excursion.

### What is the difference between the 5-day and 11-day tours?

The five-day itinerary concentrates on Bogota, Guatavita, Zipaquira and Cartagena. The eleven-day trip adds the coffee region, San Andrés and other parts of the country.

## Bogota in 6 hours: La Candelaria's museums and Mount Monserrate

If you have one full day to explore [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/)'s history, it makes sense to divide it between La Candelaria's neighbourhoods and panoramic views from Monserrate. **Ada Tours' private six-hour excursion** brings these experiences together: pre-Columbian gold, colonial architecture, twentieth-century art and views over Colombia's modern capital.

This is a separate excursion product with a confirmed duration of **6 hours**, private transport and **an English-speaking guide**. We also offer a five-hour Bogota city tour, but the two programmes differ in their included services. Compare the specific terms before choosing.

## La Candelaria: starting in the historic centre

[La Candelaria](/colombia/place/bogota/) is Bogota's old district of narrow streets, historic facades, university buildings and museums. It is one of the best places to see how the city evolved from a colonial settlement into the capital of a large country.

The route leads to the **Gold Museum**, which houses archaeological finds from cultures that inhabited what is now Colombia before the Spanish arrived. Gold objects stand alongside ceramics and other artefacts that shed light on rituals, crafts and everyday life. A highlight is the Muisca gold raft associated with the legend of El Dorado.

After the Gold Museum, the programme visits **Casa de la Moneda**, the historic Mint, and the **Botero Museum**. Works by Fernando Botero reveal a different era of Colombian art, while the Mint tells the story of the country's money and urban history. Visits to all three museums are explicitly included in this itinerary.

## Plaza Bolivar: the city's political centre

The next stage passes through Plaza Bolivar, surrounded by the cathedral and government and administrative buildings; Casa de Nariño is nearby. What makes the historic centre remarkable is how major events in the city's history and architecture from different periods are represented in adjoining streets.

The private format lets you ask your guide questions about Colombian history and focus on topics of interest. However, the six hours cover **several museums and Monserrate**, so spending several hours exploring every museum collection is not automatically part of the programme.

## Monserrate: rising above Bogota

The itinerary ends at [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/), the mountain above eastern Bogota. Its summit stands more than 3,000 metres above sea level; from here you can see the capital's neighbourhoods extending across the mountain valley. There is also a well-known religious sanctuary at the summit.

**The ascent of Monserrate is included.** The programme does not specify the means of ascent: both a cable car and funicular operate on the mountain, but the transport choice and technical arrangements should be confirmed for the travel date. A self-guided climb up the mountain trail should not be assumed to be a mandatory part of this six-hour excursion.

Because of Bogota's and Monserrate's altitude, it is worth moving at a relaxed pace, especially during the first days after flying in. Mountain weather changes quickly, and clouds may limit the view from the top.

## What is included and what costs extra

| Included element | Terms |
|---|---|
| Format | Private, 6 hours |
| Transport | Private |
| Guiding | English-speaking guide |
| Museums | Admission tickets included |
| Monserrate | Ascent included |
| Insurance | Local medical insurance card |

**Lunch and dinner are not included.** No separate price for the standalone six-hour excursion is given on this page; it must not be inferred from another city tour or a longer travel package.

For the guide language, note that English is the only confirmed option for this excursion. Russian-speaking guides being available on other capital city tours does not mean they are automatically included here.

## On which days are museums open?

The museums follow different schedules. According to official Banco de la República information, **the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays**, while **the Botero Museum and Casa de la Moneda are closed on Tuesdays**. These details are also noted in our excursion terms.

If your travel date falls on a museum closure day, the standard visiting order cannot work without changes. Confirm the date, open exhibitions and possible sequence before finalising the route. Holiday closures may also differ from the normal weekly schedule.

## When to choose this itinerary

The six-hour programme suits travellers who want to explore the main historical collections and finish their introduction to the city with a mountain panorama. If you only want a short tour of the streets and central squares, compare other [Bogota excursions](/colombia/bogota/) and their durations.

This excursion forms part of the [eight-day "Season of Colours" journey](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/), combining Bogota, Chicáque Park and the Caño Cristales area. In the larger tour, the capital's cultural section introduces the trip before its natural landscapes. Travellers on the full tour should check their included itinerary first to avoid booking the same excursion day twice.

## Frequently asked questions about the six-hour Bogota excursion

### Which museums are included in the six-hour route?

The Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum. Admission is included, along with the ascent of Monserrate.

### What language is the excursion conducted in?

It is accompanied by **an English-speaking guide**. Another language must be arranged separately.

### Can you choose Monday or Tuesday?

Under normal schedules, the Gold Museum is closed on Monday, while the Botero Museum and Mint are closed on Tuesday. If the trip falls on those days, the visiting programme must change or another date be chosen.

### Is lunch included in the price?

No. Lunch and dinner are expressly listed among the services that are not included.

### How does the six-hour excursion differ from the five-hour one?

Both introduce Bogota, but **the six-hour product** specifically confirms private transport, an English-speaking guide, tickets to three museums, the Monserrate ascent and a medical insurance card. Check the five-hour tour's own page for its terms.

## Tours featuring the six-hour Bogota museums and Monserrate excursion

The [six-hour Bogota excursion](/colombia/bogota/bogota-museums-monserrate-6-hours/) combines a walk through La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, Casa de la Moneda, Botero Museum, Plaza Bolivar and an ascent of Monserrate. ## How the excursion fits into the Caño Cristales journey

On the [“Season of Colours: Bogota and Caño Cristales in 8 Days” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/), day 1 is dedicated to arrival and check-in in [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/). The **second day** includes a six-hour city excursion with museums and Monserrate.

Next, the route continues to Chicáque Cloud Forest. Travellers then fly to [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/), travel along the Guayabero River and visit natural areas around [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/). The capital's museums and culture therefore introduce a journey whose main experiences are tropical forest and the river's extraordinary colours.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_colombia_cano_cristales_8_days}}

The eight-day programme includes 7 nights, with accommodation in Bogota and the La Manigua nature lodge in La Macarena. The tour specifically lists the Bogota–La Macarena–Bogota flight, transfers and scheduled excursions among its inclusions. International airfare is not included.

## Six hours in Bogota: museums and city panorama

The route starts in historic La Candelaria and passes through museums devoted to different periods in Colombia's history. The Gold Museum houses pre-Columbian artefacts, Casa de la Moneda explores monetary and urban history, and the Botero Museum displays paintings and sculptures.

After Plaza Bolivar, the programme concludes with an ascent of Monserrate, offering expansive views of [Bogota](/colombia/place/bogota/) and the surrounding mountains.

| Excursion stage | What is included |
|---|---|
| Historic centre | Guided walk |
| Museums | Admission tickets |
| Monserrate | Mountain ascent |
| Transport | Private vehicle |

The [standalone six-hour product](/colombia/bogota/bogota-museums-monserrate-6-hours/) confirms private transport, an English-speaking guide, tickets to the named museums, an ascent of Monserrate and a local medical insurance card. Lunch and dinner are not included.

According to the programme, the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays, while Casa de la Moneda and the Botero Museum are closed on Tuesdays. Check opening times for your chosen date before finalising the excursion sequence.

## How the six-hour excursion differs from the five-hour one

The [five-hour Bogota sightseeing excursion](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/) also covers La Candelaria, the main museums and Monserrate. However, the five-hour tour includes transfers and an English-speaking guide, whereas the six-hour programme additionally lists admission tickets and a local medical insurance card.

It would be misleading to compare the two offers by their attractions alone. Consider the duration, included services and **which exact excursion is built into your chosen multi-day tour**. For the trip to Caño Cristales, we offer the six-hour excursion, so refer to its specific terms.

## When is the best time to visit Caño Cristales?

The [“Season of Colours” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/) is scheduled for the season **from 1 June to 30 November 2027**, according to the current programme. Charter flights to La Macarena are specified from Monday through Thursday; access to certain river sections depends on permits from the conservation authorities and weather.

This differs from urban attractions, which may be visited year-round subject to museum opening days. When selecting dates, first check whether the nature section of the route is possible, then coordinate your museum day in Bogota.

For comparisons of nature and cultural trips in the country, see the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/). Further geographical information about the capital is available on the [Bogota page](/colombia/place/bogota/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring the six-hour Bogota excursion

### On which day is the excursion scheduled?

On the eight-day Caño Cristales programme, it takes place on day two, after arrival and before the trip to Chicáque Cloud Forest.

### Are museum admission tickets included?

The six-hour excursion includes tickets to the Gold Museum, Mint and Botero Museum, as well as the ascent of Monserrate.

### Are meals included in the excursion?

Lunch and dinner are not included. Meals on other days are governed by the multi-day tour terms.

### Can you visit Caño Cristales in any month?

The tour specifies dates from June through November 2027. Actual river access depends on the season, weather and decisions by the protected area's administration.

The programmes differ in duration and included services. It is better to choose based on the time you actually have, your interest in museums and whether you want to travel into the mountains around the capital. Bogota's geography and principal sights are described separately on the [city page](/colombia/place/bogota/).

The [five-hour Bogota city tour](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/) includes La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, Botero Museum, Plaza Bolivar and Monserrate. Transfers and an English-speaking guide are included; lunch is paid for separately.

There is also a shorter [five-hour excursion just to the Salt Cathedral](/colombia/zipaquira/zipaquira-salt-cathedral-5-hours/) without a confirmed visit to Guatavita.

## La Candelaria, the Gold Museum and the Botero Museum

**La Candelaria** is Bogota's historic district, home to colonial buildings, squares and museums. During the excursion, travellers explore architecture and collections that bring the region's history before and after the Spanish conquest to life.

The **Gold Museum** displays archaeological finds from Colombia's different Indigenous cultures. The official Visit Bogotá tourism portal particularly highlights the famous Muisca gold raft, associated with the origins of the El Dorado legend. The museum is far more than an exhibition of precious metal: its objects tell stories of rituals, craftsmanship and the beliefs of ancient societies.

The **Botero Museum** introduces the paintings and sculpture of Fernando Botero. Excursions also feature Casa de la Moneda, the old Mint. Plaza Bolivar completes an introduction to the capital's political and architectural centre, with the cathedral and important public buildings surrounding it.

If **included admission tickets** matter, choose the [private six-hour programme](/colombia/bogota/bogota-museums-monserrate-6-hours/), which explicitly lists them. The separate five-hour city tour must not automatically be assumed to offer the same terms.

## Monserrate: views across the city from above

[Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/) rises in the eastern mountains above Bogota. Its summit offers a broad panorama of the city and surrounding mountain valley. A religious sanctuary stands here, so Monserrate combines natural scenery with cultural history.

The mountain can be reached in different ways, including by cable car or funicular. But the precise transport and tickets depend on **the excursion you select**. The ascent is included in our six-hour excursion's services; for other programmes, check their individual descriptions.

The altitude is far higher than in many European cities: Bogota itself sits in the Andes, and Monserrate rises higher still. Some travellers may prefer to take the first hours slowly and consider their response to high altitude.

## Guatavita and the Salt Cathedral: outside the city

[Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) is associated with stories of Muisca rituals and the El Dorado legend. Visitors come for the mountain scenery and history of pre-Columbian beliefs. The eight-hour itinerary includes a walk around the lake, a stop in [Guatavita town](/colombia/place/guatavita-town/) and a transfer to Zipaquira.

**Zipaquira Salt Cathedral** was built inside a former salt mine at a depth of approximately **180 metres**. Visitors follow underground passages and chambers with architectural features and lighting. It is an entirely different way to experience Colombia from a walk through La Candelaria.

To visit both attractions in one outing, choose the [eight-hour Guatavita + Zipaquira excursion](/colombia/bogota/zipaquira-guatavita-tour-from-bogota/). If the mine itself is your main interest and time is limited, the [five-hour group excursion to the Salt Cathedral](/colombia/zipaquira/zipaquira-salt-cathedral-5-hours/) is a better fit.

## Choosing an itinerary and confirming the details

In the capital, allow for city traffic and museum schedules. When planning our six-hour excursion, remember that **the Gold Museum is closed on Mondays**, while **the Botero Museum and Mint are closed on Tuesdays**. Check these schedules for your travel date, as museum opening arrangements can change.

Weather at Monserrate and high-altitude Guatavita may be cooler than sunny photographs suggest. Take a windbreaker, comfortable shoes and time for an unhurried walk. When visiting Zipaquira underground, consider the stairs, lighting and individual comfort in enclosed spaces.

To compare programmes and plan a journey through several cities, see the [Colombia tours catalogue](/colombia/tour/) and [excursions around the country](/colombia/excursion/). Refer to the exact product page: **the five-hour city tour, private six-hour programme and excursions to Zipaquira are distinct products**.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions in Bogota

### What should you choose on your first day in the capital?

For an introduction to the city, choose the [La Candelaria, museums and Monserrate city tour](/colombia/bogota/bogota-city-tour/). It focuses on Bogota itself, while Zipaquira and Guatavita are outside the city.

### How is the six-hour Bogota excursion different?

The [private six-hour option](/colombia/bogota/bogota-museums-monserrate-6-hours/) specifically includes transport, tickets to the listed museums, the ascent of Monserrate and a local medical insurance card.

### Can you combine the Salt Cathedral and Guatavita?

Yes, both are included in the [eight-hour excursion from Bogota](/colombia/bogota/zipaquira-guatavita-tour-from-bogota/). The five-hour Salt Cathedral trip is a separate product.

### Are meals included on city excursions?

Lunch is paid for separately on the five-hour tour, while lunch and dinner are excluded from the private six-hour tour. For other excursions, check their individual terms.

### What if a museum is closed on your chosen day?

Check museum hours before booking and agree whether the visiting order or date can be changed. Do not count on guaranteed admission to an exhibition when it is closed.
